questions.q: Why do public groups exist, per this lesson?
options: They are a named, reusable recipient that sharing rules and other group-based grants can point at
They replace the need for profiles and permission sets
They are only used for report folder permissions, nothing else
They automatically become queues once they reach 10 members
questions.explain: Public groups are the reusable, named bundle of members that sharing rules (and other features) target, built once and reused.

questions.q: What can a public group contain as members, per this lesson?
options: Only individual users, nothing else
Users, roles, roles and subordinates, and even other public groups, nested arbitrarily
Only queues
Only other public groups, never individual users
questions.explain: The lesson states a group can contain users, roles, roles and subordinates, and other public groups, nested arbitrarily.

questions.q: What problem does a Queue solve that a Public Group doesn't, per this lesson?
options: Queues set field-level security for a group of users
Queues are a holding location for unassigned records, with members who accept and work them -- distribution, not just visibility
Queues replace organization-wide defaults
Queues control login hours for their members
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes queues as solving workload distribution (holding and claiming unassigned records), not just visibility.

questions.q: In the lesson's framing, what question does a Public Group answer versus what question does a Queue answer?
options: Both answer the exact same question
Public Group answers who should be able to SEE something; Queue answers who's responsible for WORKING it
Public Group answers who's responsible for working it; Queue answers who can see it
Neither relates to access or workflow at all
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly frames public groups around visibility and queues around distribution/responsibility.

questions.q: What interaction pattern does adding members to a Queue use, per this lesson?
options: A drag-and-drop canvas unique to queues
The same Available/Selected, Add/Remove picker pattern used for roles, groups, and manual sharing
A criteria-based rule builder
Direct edits to the role hierarchy tree
questions.explain: The lesson notes Queue Members reuses the same picker pattern seen throughout the chapter for granting access to specific users or groups.
